about: Camera capture for people and agents: list, configure, capture and record cameras.

args.help: Camera: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one)
args.name: camera

args.help: Turn the camera's auto exposure, gain and white balance off, keeping their values
args.name: off

args.help: Keep adjusting: the camera's continuous auto exposure, or Capturefab's in a session
args.name: continuous

args.help: How long settling may take
args.name: timeout

args.help: Meter only this part of the frame: X,Y,W,H as fractions 0..1
args.name: region

args.help: The longest exposure, as against motion blur: gain rises past it
args.name: max_exposure

args.help: Keep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone)
args.name: keep

result.by: camera|capturefab — whose auto exposure settled or runs: the camera's own (ExposureAuto Once or Continuous), or Capturefab's (with --region, --max-exposure, or when the camera has none)
result.iterations: int — exposure and gain changes made; by the camera, how often it was asked whether it was done
result.job: {id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}} — with --continuous by capturefab: the session job it runs as, which jobs stop ends
result.limited_by: exposure_max|exposure_min|gain_max|camera|timeout — what stopped it short of the target
result.mean: float — mean brightness 0..1 at the end
result.settled: bool — brightness reached its target, or a limit; false is still exit 0

auto.summary: Settle exposure and gain, then hold them; or turn auto exposure off or on

args.help: Camera, repeatable: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one)

args.help: Time between frames of a time lapse, with -n or --for

args.help: Change settings first, as one atomic change (as set does); repeatable

result.after_change: true — frames exposed before the camera's last settings change were let pass
result.bandwidth_mbps: float — with -c repeated, for GigE cameras that share a host network interface: the rate this one was paced to, its share of the interface (a warning when it could not be paced)
result.bit_depth: int — bits per sample in the files: 16 for PNG of Mono10..Mono16 (samples at the top bits, sBIT says how many count), every bit for raw, else 8
result.cameras: [{camera,files,count,truncated?,width,height,pixel_format,bit_depth,source_bits?,settings,time,device_ts_ns?,frames,dropped,incomplete?,resent?,duration_s?,fps?,first_id?,last_id?,gaps?,consecutive?,after_change?,warmup_ms?,settled?,bandwidth_mbps?,warnings?,inspect?,dry_run?,output?,format?,every_s?,first_at?,ends_at?,auto?}] — with -c repeated: one result per camera; in error details, a failed camera's {camera,error,files?,truncated?,job?}
result.consecutive: bool — a burst's frames follow one another with no frame missing
result.device_ts_ns: int — the camera's clock when the first frame was taken (GigE, U3V, sim); never a date
result.dropped: int — frames lost while it ran: the encoders' queue was full, or the transport lost them
result.duration_s: float — first to last frame, for several
result.ends_at: string — with --dry-run, for a time lapse
result.every_s: float — with --dry-run, for a time lapse
result.files: [string] — absolute paths, in order; at most 1000, the rest counted in truncated
result.first_id: int — a burst's first frame's block ID
result.fps: float — frames per second from the first frame to the last, by the camera's clock when it has one
result.frames: int — frames the camera delivered while the capture ran, including those let pass
result.gaps: int — block IDs missing between a burst's first and last frame
result.incomplete: int — frames that arrived incomplete, where the transport counts them
result.inspect: {exposure,verdict,suggest?,focus?,preview?} — with --inspect: the last frame measured as inspect measures it
result.job: {id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}} — with --background, as jobs lists it, once armed or its first frame is saved
result.last_id: int — a burst's last frame's block ID
result.output: "-" — with -o -: the image went to stdout
result.passthrough: true — the JPEG files are the ones the source sent (an MJPEG webcam, stream or file), as they were, with the provenance comment: not decoded and encoded again
result.resent: int — packets the camera sent again, where the transport counts them
result.settings: {exposure_us?,auto_exposure?,gain_db?,gain?,auto_gain?,auto_wb?,fps?,trigger?,black_level?,gamma?,binning?,offset_x?,offset_y?,reverse_x?,reverse_y?} — the camera's settings when the first frame was taken, as the camera has them; trigger: off, or its source (software, line0)
result.settled: false — its exposure was still changing when --warmup ran out (with a warning)
result.skew_ms: int — with -c repeated: how far apart the cameras' first frames arrived; all were armed first and asked for a frame at the same moment
result.source_bits: int — the camera's bits per sample, when the files keep fewer (color or Bayer PNG, JPEG)
result.time: string — RFC 3339 time of the first frame
result.truncated: int — files saved but not listed
result.warmup_ms: int — how long a camera that sets its own exposure took to settle after it started

capture.summary: Save frames: one shot, a burst, a time lapse or a delayed capture; never overwrites

result.script: string — with --json: the completion script; without it, the script alone

result.after_change: true — frames exposed before the camera's last settings change were let pass
result.dropped: int — frames the transport lost meanwhile, where it counts them
result.exposure: {mean,p1,p50,p99,clipped_low,clipped_high,clipped_low_px?,clipped_high_px?,max?} — brightness 0..1; shares and counts of pixels at black and at full scale, counted over every pixel of the region at the camera's bit depth; max: the brightest sample as a share of full scale
result.focus: {sharpness} — variance of the Laplacian over the region; compare between frames of one camera and scene (-v adds tenengrad, brenner, variance)
result.frame: {width,height,pixel_format,bits?,id?,device_ts_ns?,time,age_ms} — the frame measured, taken after the command began: its block ID and the camera's clock (ns, never a date) where the transport has them, and when it arrived
result.frames: int — frames received for this inspection, the one measured included
result.incomplete: int — frames that arrived incomplete meanwhile, where the transport counts them
result.preview: string — the preview image's path; absent with --preview none
result.resent: int — packets the camera sent again meanwhile, where the transport counts them
result.series: [{t,sharpness,mean}] — with --for: every sample, t in seconds from the first; the other fields describe the sharpest frame
result.settled: false — its exposure was still changing when --warmup ran out (verdict not_settled, with a warning)
result.suggest: {ev,exposure_us?,limited_by?:exposure_max|exposure_min|clipped} — how far to move exposure, in stops, toward mid-grey without clipping highlights; absent when close enough. clipped: most of the frame is clipped, so this is a first step; inspect again
result.warmup_ms: int — how long a camera that sets its own exposure took to settle after it started
result.warnings: [string] — such as a camera still settling when --warmup ran out (verdict not_settled)

conventions.camera: -c/--camera CAM (CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA). Without it: the session's only camera, else the only camera list finds (not sim: or screens)
conventions.describe: capturefab schema COMMAND: arguments, result fields and errors
conventions.globals: --json, -q/--quiet, -v/--verbose, --session NAME (CAPTUREFAB_SESSION), --no-session (overrides it); before or after the command
conventions.jobs: capture/record block until done; --background prints a job instead (jobs wait ID). Ctrl-C: capture exits 130 with details.files; open-ended record ends normally
conventions.json: --json (or CAPTUREFAB_JSON=1): one line on stdout, the result on exit 0, else {"error":{code,message,hint?,details?}}: code is the reason (see errors), the exit code its category. No nulls; warnings ≤10
conventions.results: snake_case keys; units in names (exposure_us); times RFC 3339 UTC; lists bounded with truncated
conventions.routing: --session NAME, else a session holding the camera, else the auto session, open 60s after last use (--keep DUR); --keep 0 or --no-session: a worker of the command
conventions.streams: NDJSON: watch a line per measurement, shell per command; capture, record, jobs wait --progress: stderr lines {progress:{job,state,saved,planned?,elapsed_s,left_s?,…}}

errors.meaning: the operation failed
invalid arguments or input
not a valid duration (see grammars.duration)
no such feature or control; see details.did_you_mean
outside the feature's range; details {feature,value,min,max,inc,nearest,unit}
not one of details.choices
the feature is read-only
another setting locks the feature now; see details.locked_by
several cameras match; pick one of details.candidates with -c
no camera matches; details.candidates lists what answered
another process or job holds the camera; details.held_by when known
the OS refused access; see hint
the camera went away
the camera worker process died
no running session has that name
FFmpeg could not be found or started
the camera, stream or service cannot be reached
the camera needs a sign-in; run login add
the camera refused the sign-in
no frame arrived in time
a triggered camera got no trigger in time; details.trigger
the operation did not finish in time
the camera or this build cannot do that
the output exists (never overwritten); details.path
disk full or below CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE; details {path,free_bytes?}
fewer results than requested; see details
stopped by a signal; details hold partial results

grammars.selector: list id (gige:…, u3v:…, avfoundation:…, v4l2:…, dshow:…), serial, IPv4, rtsp(s)://, srt://, http(s)://, onvif://host[/path], file, sim:N[?drop=0..0.5&line0=every:DUR], sim:replay:PATH
grammars.template: -o: {camera} {serial} {seq} {seq:N} {time} {date} {tag:KEY} {ext}; a folder holds {camera}-{time}-{seq}.{ext}; a taken name fails without {seq}, {time} or --on-exists number
